title: Soldier's Enchanted Avocado Harvest Simulation
description: A soldier navigates a mystical sunlit grove to collect enchanted avocados scattered across the terrain. The player controls the soldier's patrol path through waypoints, adjusts the intensity and direction of volumetric god rays to reveal hidden avocados, and must harvest a target number before a timer expires.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) implementing an interactive harvest simulation. Load three GLB assets: soldier.glb as the player character with walk animation, godrays_demo.glb as the environment providing a mystical sunlit backdrop, and Avocado.glb spawned 8 times at random positions on a ground plane within the scene bounds. Setup: Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0,8,15) looking at the origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and a DirectionalLight representing the sun (intensity 1.5) that casts shadows. Place the godrays_demo scene centrally as the environment. Scale avocados to roughly 8x their default size so they are visible. The soldier should be scaled appropriately and placed at a start position. Interactions (6-10 steps with validation): 1) Click anywhere on the ground plane to set a waypoint; validate the click intersects the ground using raycasting. 2) The soldier animates and walks toward the waypoint using lerp-based movement; validate the soldier reaches within 0.5 units before stopping. 3) When the soldier is within 1.5 units of an avocado, a 'Harvest' button appears in an HTML overlay; validate proximity before enabling. 4) Clicking Harvest removes that avocado from the scene and increments a score counter displayed in a HUD. 5) A slider control (range 0-360) rotates the DirectionalLight around the Y axis, changing god ray shadow angles; validate the slider value maps correctly to light rotation. 6) A second slider (range 0.2-3.0) adjusts the DirectionalLight intensity, simulating time-of-day; validate the range is clamped. 7) Two avocados are initially hidden (visible=false) and only become visible when light intensity exceeds 2.0, simulating magical reveal. 8) A 90-second countdown timer is displayed; when it reaches zero, disable all interactions and show a results panel with the final score. Use AnimationMixer for the soldier walk cycle. Render loop via requestAnimationFrame updating mixer, soldier movement, and timer. Include a clean HTML/CSS HUD overlay showing score, timer, and slider controls.
